title: Punkia
description: The corporate-fog chamber of QOOBIX, built to diagnose alignment loops, dashboard possession, AI theatre, meeting addiction, family-culture guilt, meritocracy residue, and management language that has lost contact with oxygen.

intro.title: Corporate fog exposure scan
intro.body: Proteus has entered the meeting room wearing protective gloves. Punkia will inspect alignment phrases, dashboards, AI claims, family-culture guilt, fake agility, and other airborne nonsense before it learns your job title.

questions.question: When someone says “let’s align”, what is often happening in fog conditions?

answers.text: Nobody wants to own the decision yet.
The organisation has achieved spiritual harmony.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. The decision has entered witness protection.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Comfortable answer detected. Punkia has placed it in a jar labelled “sounds professional, does nothing”.
questions.realityCheck: Alignment without ownership is just group fog. A useful alignment conversation ends with a decision, an owner, a deadline, and something that changes outside the room.
questions.practicalMove: Ask: “Who owns the decision, what changes after this meeting, and what deadline exists outside the slide deck?”

questions.question: What is a dashboard most likely to become in a confused organisation?

answers.text: A shrine to numbers nobody acts on.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. The dashboard is driving. The adult appears to have left the vehicle.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. The rectangle is glowing, but nobody has proved it can make a decision.
questions.realityCheck: A dashboard is useful only when someone acts on the signal. Otherwise it is wallpaper with percentages.
questions.practicalMove: For each metric, ask: “What decision does this change, who acts on it, and what happens if it moves?”

questions.question: What is the clearest sign of AI theatre?

answers.text: The word intelligence appears before the use case.
The team knows what error looks like.
The demo contains fewer adjectives than results.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. A pitch deck just became nervous.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: AI theatre detected. The machine may be real; the claim has already ordered smoke effects.
questions.realityCheck: AI is useful when it improves a defined task with measurable trade-offs. AI theatre starts when the vocabulary grows faster than the mechanism.
questions.practicalMove: Ask: “What job does this do, what does it replace or improve, how do we measure error, and who is responsible when it fails?”

questions.question: What is fake agility?

answers.text: Moving quickly without deciding what matters.
Using sticky notes with emotional confidence.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. Agility without priorities is panic with ceremonies.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. Punkia has found a sprint board and no adult supervision.
questions.realityCheck: Agility is not constant motion. It is the ability to change direction because evidence justified the change.
questions.practicalMove: Ask: “What priority remains stable, what evidence would change it, and what work must stop?”

questions.question: What does “let’s circle back” often mean when oxygen is low?

answers.text: We have a clear next step.
We are postponing discomfort and calling it process.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. The circle has no exit and has requested budget.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. The phrase has begun reproducing in the calendar.
questions.realityCheck: Some follow-ups are useful. But circle-back language often hides a missing owner, unclear decision, or fear of saying no.
questions.practicalMove: Ask: “What specific question remains open, who will answer it, and when will a decision be made?”

questions.question: What is transparency theatre?

answers.text: Sharing useful information with the right people.
Announcing openness while hiding the actual constraints.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. The window is large. The truth is still in storage.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. Transparency is not the same as making fog visible.
questions.realityCheck: Transparency matters only when people can see the relevant facts, constraints, trade-offs, and decision logic.
questions.practicalMove: Ask: “What information is missing, what decision does it affect, and who is allowed to act on it?”

questions.question: When a workplace says “we are like a family”, what should be inspected first?
questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. Family language often arrives just before unpaid emotional labour.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Careful. The word family has entered the room holding a timesheet and avoiding eye contact.
questions.realityCheck: Workplaces can be humane without pretending employment is kinship. Family language often blurs boundaries around time, loyalty, disagreement, and compensation.
questions.practicalMove: Ask: “What does this expectation require, is it paid, is it optional, and what boundary protects the employee?”

questions.question: What is ownership without authority?
questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. Ownership without authority is blame in a motivational costume.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. The responsibility has arrived. The power is still in another building.
questions.realityCheck: Accountability only works when authority, resources, information, and decision rights are aligned with the responsibility.
questions.practicalMove: Ask: “What decisions can I make, what resources can I use, and who removes blockers when authority is missing?”

questions.question: What does meritocracy mythology usually forget?

answers.text: Luck, networks, timing, bias, inherited advantage, and the plumbing.
That everyone is trying their best.
That performance reviews are sacred texts.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. The ladder was not equally placed, but the poster was very inspiring.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. The myth is wearing polished shoes and pretending the floor is level.
questions.realityCheck: Merit matters, but outcomes are shaped by context, access, visibility, timing, incentives, bias, and power.
questions.practicalMove: Ask: “What hidden advantages, constraints, or selection effects shaped this outcome before we call it pure merit?”

questions.question: What does a useful meeting leave behind?

answers.text: A decision, owner, deadline, or cancelled next meeting.
A beautiful slide with four arrows.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. A useful meeting leaves a footprint in reality.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Incorrect. The meeting has survived and is now seeking a recurring slot.
questions.realityCheck: A meeting is useful only if it changes knowledge, decisions, ownership, timing, or action.
questions.practicalMove: Before accepting a meeting, ask for the decision needed, the owner, the preparation, and the desired output.

diagnoses.title: Corporate Fog Exposure
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: You have been exposed to language that sounds professional while quietly removing the point.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that vague business phrasing may be replacing clear decisions, owners, trade-offs, and next actions.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Corporate fog works because vague language protects status, avoids conflict, and lets everyone leave the room feeling aligned with something nobody could describe under oath.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Ask: “What does this mean in observable terms, who owns it, and what changes after we say it?”
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free fog filter: The Corporate Fog Decoder can help translate the phrase before it breeds in the meeting calendar.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full antidote: The Corporate Fog Phrasebook goes deeper into business language that has lost contact with oxygen.
diagnoses.shareLine: Corporate fog is what happens when language gets promoted and meaning is made redundant.

diagnoses.title: Alignment Loop Infection
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: The organisation may be aligning because nobody wants to touch the decision without gloves.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that repeated alignment conversations are being used to postpone ownership, risk, or disagreement.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Alignment loops feel collaborative while deferring the uncomfortable moment when someone must decide, prioritise, say no, or accept consequences.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Ask: “Are we aligning on information, decision rights, priority, or accountability? Which one is unresolved?”
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free fog filter: The Corporate Fog Decoder helps spot when alignment has become a hamster wheel with catering.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full antidote: The Corporate Fog Phrasebook gives language for ending circular alignment rituals without setting fire to the room.
diagnoses.shareLine: Alignment without ownership is just group fog with minutes.

diagnoses.title: Dashboard Possession
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: The numbers are glowing. Unfortunately, nobody appears to be driving.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that metrics, dashboards, and reports may be admired more than acted upon.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Dashboards create the feeling of control because visibility looks like management. But visibility without action is surveillance of confusion.
diagnoses.practicalMove: For every metric, define the decision it changes, the threshold that triggers action, and the person responsible for responding.
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free fog filter: The Corporate Fog Decoder helps distinguish useful metrics from decorative numerology.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full antidote: The Corporate Fog Phrasebook examines dashboard worship and other rectangles of salvation.
diagnoses.shareLine: The data is driving. The driver has left the vehicle.

diagnoses.title: AI Theatre Susceptibility
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: The AI claim may contain more lighting than mechanism.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that AI language is being used to inflate a feature, decorate a pitch, or avoid explaining the actual workflow.
diagnoses.realMechanism: AI theatre works because novelty, fear, and vague technical language create a temporary authority fog around weak use cases.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Ask: “What task improves, what evidence proves it, what errors matter, and who is accountable when the machine invents confidence?”
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free fog filter: The Corporate Fog Decoder can help identify whether the AI claim has a job or merely a costume.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full antidote: The Corporate Fog Phrasebook includes sharper tools for deflating AI theatre without becoming the office pessimist.
diagnoses.shareLine: AI theatre begins when the vocabulary grows faster than the use case.

diagnoses.title: Ownership Gap
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: Responsibility has arrived wearing a badge. Authority is still on annual leave.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that someone is being held accountable for outcomes without the power, resources, information, or decision rights required to affect them.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Ownership gaps survive because they let organisations distribute blame while keeping real control elsewhere.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Ask: “What decisions can this owner actually make, what resources can they access, and who removes blockers?”
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free fog filter: The Corporate Fog Decoder helps spot when ownership is just blame with better shoes.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full antidote: The Corporate Fog Phrasebook gives sharper translations for accountability language that forgot authority.
diagnoses.shareLine: Ownership without authority is blame in a motivational costume.

diagnoses.title: Meeting Addiction
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: The organisation may be using meetings as emotional support furniture.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that meetings are being used to avoid decisions, simulate momentum, or share anxiety in scheduled rectangles.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Meetings multiply when ownership, inputs, decision criteria, and consequences are unclear. The calendar becomes a terrarium for avoidance.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Before meeting, require a purpose, decision, owner, preparation, and expected output. If none exists, cancel the ceremony.
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free fog filter: The Corporate Fog Decoder can help identify meetings that are just fog with attendance.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full antidote: The Corporate Fog Phrasebook gives phrases for escaping recurring rituals without needing a fake emergency.
diagnoses.shareLine: A useful meeting leaves a footprint in reality.

diagnoses.title: Family-Culture Guilt Event
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: The word family has appeared near labour expectations. Punkia has deployed a boundary net.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that emotional language may be used to soften, hide, or normalise unreasonable expectations.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Family-culture guilt works by replacing contractual clarity with loyalty pressure. It makes boundaries feel like betrayal.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Ask: “Is this expectation paid, optional, time-limited, and reasonable? What boundary protects the person being asked?”
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free fog filter: The Corporate Fog Decoder helps translate affectionate workplace language before it starts eating weekends.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full antidote: The Corporate Fog Phrasebook dissects family culture, loyalty pressure, and emotional invoice camouflage.
diagnoses.shareLine: If work is family, ask who controls the inheritance.

diagnoses.title: Meritocracy Myth Residue
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: The success story may have omitted the scaffolding, the luck, and several inconvenient doors.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that outcomes may be explained as pure merit while ignoring access, timing, bias, capital, networks, visibility, or inherited advantage.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Meritocracy myths are comforting because they make success look clean and failure look deserved. Reality is messier and less obedient.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Ask: “What hidden advantage, selection effect, constraint, or structural factor shaped this result before we call it merit?”
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free fog filter: The Corporate Fog Decoder helps identify fairness theatre before it becomes policy.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full antidote: The Corporate Fog Phrasebook translates meritocracy myths without removing all hope, only the propaganda.
diagnoses.shareLine: The ladder was not equally placed, but the poster was very inspiring.
